quote: 1. My longevity stems from the fact that I try to control risk as much as possible. When the market starts down I sell quickly and don't let the losses get out of hand.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 2. The key is to see things as they are—operating in the now—without seeing things as worse than they are out of fear, or better than they are out of greed.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 3. I'm only rich because I know when I'm wrong.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 4. There are only four things in trading that you can control directly: Before you make the trade, you control what you buy, how much you buy, and when you buy. After you make the trade, you control when you sell.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 5. When you re-frame cutting losses and celebrate avoiding a large loss and freeing up capital for a better trade, suddenly having discipline becomes second nature and being undisciplined becomes painful.

quote: 6. None of us have figured out a better way to manage risk, or to avoid a big decline, other than taking a small loss.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 7. Making the decision to cut your loss in a stock requires that you accept the notion that only you can be wrong; the market is never wrong.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 8. My percentage of winners is only about 50/50, because I cut my losers very quickly. The maximum loss I allow is 7%, and usually I am out of a losing stock a lot quicker. I make my money on the few stocks a year that double and triple in price. The profits in those trades easily makes up for all the small losers.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 9. The greatest thing about the market is that it is always fun to be looking for that next big winner— trying to find the stock with all the characteristics that are going to make it have a big move. To me it is like a giant treasure hunt.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 10. Soros has taught me that when you have tremendous conviction on a trade, you have to go for the jugular. It takes courage to be a pig.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 11. I make most of my mistakes if I actually start trading too early — it's amazing how some of these things gap up and then a half an hour later you're already down a couple points.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 12. Everyone makes mistakes; that's unavoidable. But not correcting a mistake or minimizing the damage of a position gone wrong is completely under your own control.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 13. Most of my big mistakes have been selling too early… great companies, I often buy too early, but I don't sell.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 14. Not losing big is the single most important factor for winning big. As a speculator, losing is not a choice, but how much you lose is.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 15. One of the most suicidal things you can do in trading is to keep adding to a losing position.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 16. What exactly are you trying to accomplish? Do you want to make money, or are you engaged in an exercise in ego to prove that, somehow, you know more than the market?
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 17. Amateurs are scared of positions that stop them out once or twice or just weary of the struggle; professionals are objective and dispassionate.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 18. Stocks should be at a profit the first day you buy them. In fact, having a profit on the first day is one of the best indicators that you are going to make money on that trade.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 19. Earnings don't move the overall market; it's the Federal Reserve Board. Focus on the central banks and focus on the movement of liquidity. Most people in the market are looking for earnings and conventional measures. It's liquidity that moves markets.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 20. The moment the price hits the stop-loss, I sell the position without question. Once I'm out of the stock, I can then evaluate the situation with a clear head.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 21. There is a lot more noise and movement in the market with high speed trading and computerized algorithms, but the stocks that have the biggest moves continue to have the same characteristics.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 22. The greatest investors make large concentrated bets where they have a lot of conviction. They're not buying 35 or 40 names and diversifying.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 23. If you are not willing to accept small losses, you will take big losses.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 24. I'm only gonna buy exactly at the buy point, exactly where the stock was coming out into new highs above the majority of the base.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 25. I strongly believe the only way to make long-term returns in our business that are superior is by being a pig.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 26. The way to build superior long-term returns is through preservation of capital and home runs.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 27. You must not risk more than you can reasonably expect to gain; otherwise, you're stacking the odds against you, and that's gambling.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 28. The difference between interest and commitment is the will not to give up. When you truly commit to something, you have no alternative but success.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 29. If you want to reap big gains in the market, make up your mind right now that you are going to separate trading from your ego. It's more important to make money than it is to be right.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 30. I've always made even higher returns in bear markets than bull markets.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 31. Always go in with a plan and approach every trade risk-first.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 32. I've learned many things from George Soros, but perhaps the most significant is that it's not whether you're right or wrong that's important, but how much money you make when you're right and how much you lose when you're wrong.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 33. The single most important advice I can give anybody is: Learn from your mistakes. That is the only way to become a successful trader.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 34. That's probably the biggest mistake investors make, is they invest in the present rather than forward-looking, and looking where the puck's going instead of where the puck is.

quote: 35. If you have to buy one of these late-stage bases, buy small positions so as not to get pummeled if they fail.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 36. The big mistakes start out as small mistakes that were allowed to get out of hand. You must realize that big losses are a choice and take responsibility for controlling them.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 37. The success I eventually achieved didn't come from natural talent. Unconditional persistence and learned discipline brought me where I am today.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 38. I think diversification and all the stuff they're teaching at business school today is probably the most misguided concept anywhere.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 39. I feel my success comes from my love of the markets. I am not a casual trader. It is my life. I have a passion for trading. It is not merely a hobby or even a career choice for me. There is no question that this is what I am supposed to do with my life.

quote: 40. If you don't have a plan, you will surely experience paralyzing emotions and second-guess yourself at key decision-making moments.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 41. You want to get on board when institutional money is pouring into a stock and lifting it significantly higher.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 42. If you find yourself getting stopped out of your positions over and over, there can only be two things wrong: 1. Your stock selection criteria are flawed. 2. The general market environment is hostile.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 43. If, during the bull phase, the leaders start losing, it indicates that a bear market is developing.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 44. It's better to lose correctly than to win incorrectly.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 45. The first thing I heard when I got in the business was, 'Bulls make money, bears make money, and pigs get slaughtered.' I'm here to tell you I was a pig.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 47. There's no silver bullet. And I'm the great beneficiary of 40 years of scars and successes that I can go back on, and a lot of pattern recognition because there's not much I haven't seen in this business.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 48. Trading without a stop-loss is like driving a car without brakes. Maybe you could make it around the block a few times, but if you did drive without brakes, how far do you think you could go before you crash?
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 49. I don't really like hedging. To me, if something needs to be hedged, you shouldn't have a position in it.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 50. Find a style that makes sense to you and fits your personality, and then commit to it fully. Don't try to become a jack of all trades, become a specialist and master a specific approach.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 51. We want to see the earnings and price and the relative strength going in the same direction.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 52. There are three basic levels of knowledge. The first level is when an idea is presented to you by someone else. The second level is when you become convinced that what you have been told is true. The third level is a knowing—the most powerful form of awareness.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 53. Instead, now there's just a bunch of computers running wild. That's really what's happened for the last few years. There's no human contact in terms of slowing the whole process down.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 54. To compound your money, and not your mistakes, your goal is to buy on the way up—not on the way down.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 56. By keeping track of your results, you will gain insight into yourself and your trading that no book, seminar, indicator, or system could ever tell you.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 57. Winning stock traders have rules and a well-thought-out plan. Conversely, losers lack rules, or if they have rules, they don't stick to them for very long; they deviate.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 58. Those who trade without a stop eventually stop trading.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 59. You make your best decisions when they're your own decisions, and you have no one else to blame.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 60. I believe the best way to manage risk is to be bullish when you have a compelling risk/reward and bearish when you don't.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 61. Every great money manager I've ever met, all they want to talk about is their mistakes. There's a great humility there.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 62. Those who succeed big at anything all have the same attitude: You keep going until it happens or you die trying. Quitting is not an option.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 63. Over the years, I've come to realize that fear is the number one emotion that causes traders to sabotage their discipline. Fear of missing out causes them to chase stocks and buy past the point at which they know they should.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 64. With every trade I make, my approach is always 'risk-first.' By thinking and acting 'risk-first,' you know exactly what you stand to lose if you're wrong, which in trading is far more important than what you stand to gain if you're right, because if you lose all your chips, the game is over.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 65. I believe that good investors are successful not because of their IQ, but because they have an investing discipline.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 66. The main thing is that you cut your loss immediately, without any vacillation.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 67. You don't have to involve yourself in every market movement. In fact, you should not attempt to. Be an exacting opportunist. Be selective and pick your entry spots very carefully. Wait until the probabilities are stacked in your favor before you act. With patience and discipline, you can profit from market opponents who are less disciplined and less capable than you are.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 68. Success in investing doesn't correlate with I.Q. once you're above the level of 125. Once you have ordinary intelligence, what you need is the temperament to control the urges that get other people into trouble in investing.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 69. If you're early on in your career and they give you a choice between a great mentor or higher pay, take the mentor every time. It's not even close. And don't even think about leaving that mentor until your learning curve peaks.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 70. I've never made a buy at a low that I didn't just feel terrible and scared to death making it. It's easy to sell at the bottom. You can go home that night and it relieves you of your nerves. When things are going down it's hard to buy them.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 71. During the consolidation phase, decreasing volume is good. If you continue to see very high volume, it is a potential top because it shows that a lot of people are getting out of the stock.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 72. The wonderful thing about our business is that it's liquid, and you can wipe the slate clean on any day.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 73. Letting losses run is the most serious mistake made by most investors.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 74. Never let a big winner turn into a loser.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 75. Never invest in the present. It's the anticipation of future earnings that moves stocks.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 76. I bought $6 billion worth of tech stocks and in six weeks I had lost $3 billion.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 77. Average up, not down.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 78. Buy stocks that are making new highs, not stocks that are making new lows.

quote: 79. Amateurs think about how much they can make; professionals think about how much they can lose.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 80. Put all your eggs in one basket and then watch the basket very carefully.

quote: 81. Cut your losses short and let your winners run.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 82. Don't try to catch a falling knife; let the stock prove itself before you buy.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 83. I look for the strongest stocks in the strongest industry groups.

quote: 84. When the facts change, I change my position quickly; the market doesn't care what I thought yesterday.

quote: 85. The mistake I'd say 98 percent of money managers and individuals make is they feel like they've got to be playing with a bunch of stuff.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 86. If you don't feel like a fool, you're not managing risk.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 87. I studied historical models of great winning stocks to ingrain in my mind what a stock looked like before it made a major move. I tried to get to the point where I was looking at the exact same things O'Neil did. He was my role model.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 88. Virtually every superperformance phase in big, winning stocks occurred while the stock price was in a definite price uptrend. In almost every case, the trend was identifiable early in the superperformance advance.

quote: 89. The only reason you can change your mind is if you're not arrogant about a position.

quote: 90. Do not, do NOT invest in the present; the present is not what moves stock prices, change does.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
